colorUsage.primary: Evergreen #386a57 action surface; always pair with --jk-primary-foreground (chalk #f5f6f2, 5.75:1). Dark mode lightens evergreen to #82c4a4 with #0f1f18 text (8.44:1). Evergreen also marks the link-tile hover border, the selected-tile border, the active nav underline, and the focus ring. --jk-radius (0.75rem) rounds controls; tiles use the app-local --ben-radius (1rem).
colorUsage.inlineLinks: Use --jk-foreground with underline; primary is not a universal link-text color. A whole-card link tile names its destination in the title and ends with an arrow, not colored text.
colorUsage.muted: Use --jk-muted-foreground for secondary text on background, card, or muted: #53625c in light (5.18:1 on cool gray #e3e8e4, 5.92:1 on chalk), #aab7b1 in dark. Chalk #f5f6f2 is the page, #fcfdfb the tile surface, cool gray #e3e8e4 the muted and secondary panel, and mint #cde6d7 a quiet accent surface, never body text.
colorUsage.border: Tiles sit on a 1px --jk-border (#d9e0db light, #2c3834 dark) with at most the app-local --ben-shadow hairline; --jk-shadow-control is none. --jk-input (#78857f light, #6b7a74 dark) is the field edge and meets 3:1 against the card (3.77:1 light, 3.54:1 dark); fields also keep a persistent label and the evergreen focus ring. Link tiles swap the border to evergreen on hover and focus; static tiles never change border.
colorUsage.status: Use destructive/success/warning with paired foreground and text or icon; never only color. Success reuses evergreen. Apricot #f6c794 is the warning surface with ink #26332f text in both modes (8.46:1): the “Needs reply” badge and the tile warning edge with the words “Needs attention”. The demo-portal strip uses the app-local apricot tint --ben-strip with --ben-strip-foreground.
colorUsage.charts: Use all five chart colors with labels or other redundant encodings; review adjacency in the rendered chart. Light: #386a57, #7fb79a, #f6c794, #9aa8a1, #26332f. Dark: #82c4a4, #4f8f72, #f6c794, #7d8b85, #eef1ec. The weekly visits chart is built in markup with --jk-chart-1 bars, a label on every day, and a written-out equivalent: “Mon 6, Tue 9, Wed 8, Thu 7, Fri 10, Sat 5, Sun closed.”
